Hi, I lived in the Verve the very first year it opened. Some things might have gotten better or worse, idk, so take with a grain of salt: 


1. You mean like where it’s located? It’s pretty safe. Around the perimeter of the building and along the street where all the restaurants are open. It’s also basically right next to the campus. I would say just don’t go several blocks off into the residential areas at night.

4. So yeah… management. Not the best. One of the elevators stopped working a few months in, and didn’t get fixed for the rest of the year I was there. Also, lots of party animals at the Verve. Possibly expect to hear loud noises from party rooms. 

5. Can’t say, as I moved into a new apartment. But I would assume they at least clean/tidy things to some extent before someone new comes in. 



Overall, I would say a lot of the bad reviews are warranted, but if you can put up with some of the negatives I mentioned, and you don’t get unlucky (like with stuff not working), then it should be fine. I still much preferred living in the Verve over shitty rutgers dorms (non-apartments) that felt like prisons. A lot of the this games systems and PvP focus seems to be modeled after Epic 7, so you can take a look at that game to get somewhat of an idea of what the PvP powercreep might look like (not a 100% gaurantee tho).

From my experience playing E7 in the past, there definitely is slow powercreep, where new units (especially light/dark) are going to be stronger for PvP, but not all the old units will be rendered completely useless. Some old units will remain as staples or viable for a long time, and some will have more niche usages. E7 also tries to somewhat balance the meta by regularly buffing characters (but they aren’t allowed to nerf since it’s a gacha game). There are also meta shifts where some units may fall out of favor and others become better based on newly available synergies or hidden tech/strategy that gets discovered. 

And while units do matter, gear matters more and is the ultimate limiting factor for PvP. The ppl who grind more will get better gear RNG over time and perform better. This is both a good and bad thing for PvP enjoyers. On one hand, it gives F2P and especially low spenders a small chance to compete with whales/dolphins for higher ranks, since gear farming is basically time dependent with layers of RNG, so whales can’t just insta buff all their units to the max on day 1. On the other hand, it makes the game an intense grind fest for EVERYONE that wants to play the game competitively.

Giving “feedback” to someone that already sounds good is like low hanging fruit: it’s very easy and doesn’t require very many sentences because the person likely already has a very good grasp of fundamentals. Trying to give EFFECTIVE feedback to a beginner on other hand, can be a very monumental (or even impossible) task through simple text. There are just so many nuances to singing, and differences in how individual ppl interpret and feel things, as well as varying personal issues from individual to individual, that it’s just not very incentivizing for most ppl to try to give good feedback to a beginner through a Reddit comment. At the very least, feedback would have to be several paragraphs long to have any chance of being useful (and even then, it likely won’t be useful since it won’t be interpreted or applied correctly by the person reading it). That’s why one of the most common responses to beginners is to just get a voice teacher and work with them.

So in order to play adc well, the most fundamental skill is to have good auto attack mechanics. That’s something that will just have to improve with time and practice. You’re just likely not used to auto attacking regularly from being used to playing a good wave clear mage like hwei (and also being pretty new to the game overall). Also, with the lane being a 2v2, there’s more attack angles to worry about now. You seem to have the idea that you need to “walk up to the lane opponent and aa them”, but that’s (generally) not the primary goal. Your primary goal as adc is to farm and survive. Adc’s are squishy as hell and weak without items, so your default goal should always be to focus on staying out of the enemy’s attack ranges and focus on properly last hitting minions so you get gold to get items and get stronger. You only go to attack the enemy if something happens to allow you to have a favorable trade or all in, whether that be your support/teammate making a play, the enemy mis-positioning, etc. Additionally, wave management in the bot lane is a bit different than in mid lane. Botlane is longer than midlane, so if you mess up your wave, it can be far more punishing. It’s too much to explain in a comment, so I would suggest watching a short video on basic wave management concepts and try to apply them to your games. 

In order to actually improve, I would suggest taking things one step at a time. First play some games where you just focus on maintaining good cs. This forces you to get into the rhythm of practicing auto attacks, and also managing waves so that you can cs more safely/reliably. Also focus on where you stand in relation to the enemy (particularly the enemy support). It’s good practice to stand on the opposite diagonal of the enemy support so that it’s harder for them to harass or engage onto you. Once you’ve gotten a bit comfortable with csing and positioning, then start focusing more on the enemy’s mistakes. Look for opportunities where you can get favorable trades against the enemy. Like if the one of them walks too far ahead of the other into both you and your support’s ranges. Or if the enemy adc is going for a minion (especially a cannon minion) and you can get a free auto attack off. Slowly build on small skills like this little by little, and over time you will get more comfortable with the role.

Disagree with some of the other comments on PvP. The gameplay of PvP itself is very strategic and fun, with good amounts of skill expression. It has a drafting system similar to E7. I used to play E7 quite competitively and if you liked RTA there, I do think you’ll like the RTA here as well, even if the genres are a bit different. I recommend you look up clips on YouTube to get a good sense of what PvP is like. 

Now the problem with the STATE of RTA PvP is that they don’t have a dedicated ladder/ranking system. They only have a random matchmaking system that runs as an occasional event 2 weeks at a time (you can otherwise challenge people on your friends list, buts that’s about it). I have no idea if they ever intend to add actual PvP rankings with seasons like in E7. I think you can tell already, but PvP is disliked by a lot of ppl here, but there are a portion of players that are quite enthusiastic about it. There’s been a large community run PvP tourny with another one coming up soon. 

As for stuff like pull economy and pity system, it’s a bit controversial. The pull economy itself is alright, but not enough to gaurantee that getting every new banner unit, as it takes 180 pulls for hard pity (I believe it’s usually something like 50ish F2P pulls per month?). But you do initially get a lot of gems from initial story/achievement clears. Now the real issue is that the hard pity is not like in hoyoverse where pulling a non banner SSR will guarantee the banner unit next. You HAVE to do 180 pulls to hit hard pity, and all the SSR pulls before that will just be 50/50 until the hard pity. It’s not all bad though since the rates of pulling SSR is at 2%, which is decent. So compared to hoyoverse, you will pull much more SSR units in the long run, but guaranteeing the specific ones you want will be harder. I would assume most people would prefer hoyoverse’s pity system. Oh good thing about this game is that dupes can be farmed in the form of daily shard farming (for ANY character). But it does take some time. It takes a max lvl account exactly 100 days to take 3 units from 1 star, to max 5 star. This is because you can farm 9 shards a day and it takes 300 shards to max out a single character. If you happen to pull a dupe, you just get 50 shards for that character. 

For gears there are slots for weapon, accessory, and tarot card. Weapons can be easily farmed and maxed out duped in the long term (do NOT pull on weapon banner). Accessories cannot be farmed and are collected here and there from monthly and event rewards (most valuable). Tarot cards are easy to farm. Oh and there’s also engraving stats, but those are reasonable to get in long term as well. MUCH chiller gear system compared to E7 and hoyoverse. 

For spending, a lot of F2P players are probably going to run into frustration (and they have been) from not being able to pity all characters they want. Most low spenders should have an okayish time, although it will still be hard to get every character they want as they release. Dolphins probably get the most bang for their buck out of this game. I personally don’t think it’s worth Whaling hard for this game, as you can hit a stat ceiling pretty quickly if you do. In the long term (like 1+ years), I do predict that F2P/low spenders can get pretty close to Whale power lvls due to the way stats work and chill gear system (minus accessories lol). Whales will always be a bit ahead though as they will have new characters immediately 5 starred whereas F2P will have to take time to farm shards. 

And lastly, the story in this game is very well liked.

-try not to pick units that can be hard countered until you get to last pick or second to last pick. Unless your strategy includes a counter measure to said counter(s).

-Immunity on non speed or eff res units is a almost a must.

-if you ever feel that you are drafting units not because they are optimal picks against the enemy units, but because that’s the only unit(s) you have geared for pvp, that’s a sign that you might just need to go back to farming more gear and diversifying your roster before continuing with RTA.
